parsed_output.answer: Mendel’s monohybrid experiment involved crossing pea plants with different traits to study how traits are inherited. He selected pea plants that produced either yellow or green seeds. When he crossed a pure yellow-seed plant (YY) with a pure green-seed plant (yy), all the offspring in the first generation (F1) had yellow seeds. This is because the yellow trait is dominant over the green trait. When these F1 plants were self-pollinated, the second generation (F2) showed a 3:1 ratio of yellow to green seeds. This demonstrated the law of dominance, where one trait (yellow) masks the other (green) in the F1 generation but both traits reappear in the F2 generation. The experiment showed that traits are inherited through discrete units (genes) and that dominant traits are expressed over recessive ones.
